profile.campus: Red Oak Campus, Compass Datacenters Dallas-Fort Worth market
profile.address: Red Oak, TX (Ellis County, southern edge of the Red Oak development campus)
profile.reading: This OpenStreetMap record is tagged individually to the city of Red Oak, Texas rather than the broader Ellis County designation used for the ten other building footprints in this cluster, and sits at the southernmost and westernmost edge of Compass Datacenters Red Oak development, a wholesale data center campus just south of the Dallas-Fort Worth core. Compass Datacenters own market materials describe this campus, part of its Dallas-Fort Worth market, as a 360 megawatt development that was still nearing completion as of the most recent site content reviewed, with a confirmed 200 million dollar expansion phase announced in April 2024 that added two buildings totaling more than 500,000 square feet. A separate July 2026 company news item states that Red Oak now hosts seven data centers total, though that figure appears to describe the city of Red Oak as a whole rather than Compass own building count specifically, so it should not be read as confirming exactly how many of the eleven OpenStreetMap footprints in this cluster are Compass-operated versus operated by other companies also active in the area. Compass Datacenters was founded in 2011 by Chris Crosby, a former Digital Realty senior executive who remains the company CEO, and completed its first data center, a 1.2 megawatt facility, in 2012. The company is headquartered in Dallas, Texas, and describes its current ownership, per its own about-us page, as Ontario Teachers Pension Plan, RedBird Capital Partners, and company management. Beyond Dallas-Fort Worth, Compass 2026 markets list includes active developments in Chicago Hoffman Estates, Northern Virginia Loudoun County, Toronto, and Milan, plus a newly broken-ground site in Meridian, Mississippi, alongside earlier markets including Minneapolis and Nashville that the company has since exited or transferred to independent ownership. Separately, and worth noting given this record proximity to the city center, Compass donated 12.6 million dollars to fund a 40,000 square foot workforce-training replica data center at 300 Houston School Road in Red Oak, operated by Texas State Technical College, whose June 2026 ribbon-cutting was widely covered locally, though that training building is a distinct facility from the wholesale buildings mapped in this cluster and should not be confused with this record. No per-building capacity, square footage, tenant, or year-built figure could be confirmed for this specific structure, and no local government permit or tax-abatement record could be retrieved from Red Oak city or Ellis County sources this session, so those figures are deliberately omitted rather than estimated from campus-wide totals.
profile.capacity_note: not published at a level this registry can confidently assign to this specific row. The campus overall has been described at various points from 2020 to 2026 as targeting up to 350 MW full build-out, but no current, confirmed, single-building or reliably-attributable campus-total figure was found, so none is applied to critical_it_mw.
profile.research_note: Only record in this cluster individually tagged to Red Oak city rather than Ellis County. Campus confirmed via compassdatacenters.com. Distinguished explicitly from the separate TSTC-operated training-replica building at 300 Houston School Road, which Compass funded but does not itself operate as a working data center. Government/tax-abatement sources could not be reached this session.

reading.body:
Compass Red Oak Campus in Ellis County, Texas is a hyperscale project in active expansion with no current published power figure. The operator announced a full build-out target of 350 MW in 2020 and has since grown the approved campus footprint from 165 acres to roughly 800 to 830 acres as of May 2026, with multiple construction phases reportedly underway and targeted for completion between 2025 and 2026. The campus comprises at least one completed one million square foot building alongside additional phases, though the specific megawatt capacity of any individual phase or the current operating total remains unpublished at a level this registry can reliably assign.

Without a published current power figure, this campus ranks outside the top 18 published capacity sites in Texas and cannot be placed in the state's confirmed capacity share, which totals 468 MW across 18 facilities. Texas has 133 mapped data center facilities overall, and the lack of published specifications from the majority of these sites means that operating capacity and the true scale of the state's infrastructure remain largely hidden from public view.

The campus sits on land Compass purchased between 2019 and 2023 and received 830 acre expansion approval in May 2026 amid local opposition and community engagement efforts. No specific megawatt allocation can be derived from published specifications for this particular mapped row, which sits at the southern edge of a multi-building campus where two different building naming conventions are used in trade press and aggregator sources, creating ambiguity about which of the registry's 11 tracked rows corresponds to which phase or address. The operator was acquired by Brookfield Infrastructure Partners and Ontario Teachers Pension Plan in June 2023 for 5.5 billion dollars.
